transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Most likely, yes. A small amount of clean water left down in the sump underneath the filter after a programme is normal on a dishwasher; it helps keep the pump and seals from drying out. It is not normally a sign that it has failed to drain. It would be worth investigating only if the water is dirty or smelly, rises above the filter/base, or the machine leaves dishes wet with food debris. 1. With the dishwasher switched off, lift out the filter and check the water level. A small pool below the filter level—roughly a cup or so—is normal.
2. Rinse the filter and wipe any food or greasy sludge from the sump. A partial blockage can make it leave more water than usual.
3. If there is standing water above the filter, check the drain hose behind the machine is not kinked. As it is newly installed, also have the installer check that the blanking plug was removed from the sink-waste connection. Is the water clean and only below the filter level, or is it dirty and sitting higher up?
Thanks. The water is clean and only covers the bottom of the sump under the filter, roughly a cupful. None in the main tub. The filter is clean too.

That is normal and indicates it is draining properly. A cupful of clean water contained below the filter, with none left in the main tub, is the small residual amount kept in the sump to protect the pump and seals. No further check or repair is needed. Only investigate if it becomes dirty or smelly, rises above the filter level, remains in the tub, or the dishwasher starts stopping with a drain warning.
